ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Peat, also called grass peat or peat coal, is a substance accumulated over a long period from incompletely decomposed organic remains (mainly plant remains). It mainly forms in swamp areas. The development of peat depends on the growth amount of swamp plants and the decomposition amount of remains. Peat that is still accumulating in modern swamp lands is called exposed peat. Read the distribution of exposed peat in China (Figure 1) and the changes over time in decomposition rates of different types of plants at a certain place (Figure 2). <image1> Peat has many uses and can produce huge economic benefits. A certain place is preparing to carry out a peat production experiment with a certain plant. Overall, which plant planted in this place has the best benefits?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The left side of the figure is a schematic map of "distribution of exposed peat in China", showing exposed peat distributed as points in many places in China, especially related to wetland and swamp environments. The right side is a curve graph of "decomposition rates of different plants changing with time"; the horizontal axis is January to December, the vertical axis is decomposition rate, and the legend lists plants such as reed, sedge, swamp willow, and Eriophorum. The decomposition rates of the various plants generally show seasonal changes, being higher near summer and lower at the beginning and end of the year, and different curves have different annual decomposition intensities. Then reason: The stem explains that peat is formed by long-term accumulation of incompletely decomposed plant remains, and peat development depends on plant growth amount and remains decomposition amount; therefore, a plant with good production benefits should satisfy "large biomass, relatively small decomposition loss of remains, and much net organic matter accumulation". According to Figure 2, plants with overall high within-year decomposition rates and unfavorable remains preservation can be excluded; at the same time, combined with the characteristics of reed among swamp plants as vigorous in growth, high in yield, and large in biomass, the net organic matter accumulation of reed is more favorable for forming peat. From the perspective of overall economic benefits, reed should be selected.

raw_record.original_question:
泥炭又称草炭或泥煤,是未完全分解的有机残体(主要是植物残体)长期积累起来的物质。主要形成于沼泽地区。泥炭的发育,取决于沼泽植物的生长量和残体的分解量。现代沼泽地仍在积累着的泥炭,叫裸露泥炭。读我国裸露泥炭分布(图1)和某地不同类型植物分解率随时间变化(图2)。

<image1>

泥炭具有多种用途,能产生巨大经济效益。某地准备进行某种植物的泥炭生产试验。从总体上说,该地种植何种植物效益最好？
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: The left side of the figure is a schematic map of "distribution of exposed peat in China", showing exposed peat distributed as points in many places in China, especially related to wetland and swamp environments. The right side is a curve graph of "decomposition rates of different plants changing with time"; the horizontal axis is January to December, the vertical axis is decomposition rate, and the legend lists plants such as reed, sedge, swamp willow, and Eriophorum. The decomposition rates of the various plants generally show seasonal changes, being higher near summer and lower at the beginning and end of the year, and different curves have different annual decomposition intensities. Then reason: The stem explains that peat is formed by long-term accumulation of incompletely decomposed plant remains, and peat development depends on plant growth amount and remains decomposition amount; therefore, a plant with good production benefits should satisfy "large biomass, relatively small decomposition loss of remains, and much net organic matter accumulation". According to Figure 2, plants with overall high within-year decomposition rates and unfavorable remains preservation can be excluded; at the same time, combined with the characteristics of reed among swamp plants as vigorous in growth, high in yield, and large in biomass, the net organic matter accumulation of reed is more favorable for forming peat. From the perspective of overall economic benefits, reed should be selected.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Peat, also called grass peat or peat coal, is a substance accumulated over a long period from incompletely decomposed organic remains (mainly plant remains). It mainly forms in swamp areas. The development of peat depends on the growth amount of swamp plants and the decomposition amount of remains. Peat that is still accumulating in modern swamp lands is called exposed peat. Read the distribution of exposed peat in China (Figure 1) and the changes over time in decomposition rates of different types of plants at a certain place (Figure 2).

<image1>

Peat has many uses and can produce huge economic benefits. A certain place is preparing to carry out a peat production experiment with a certain plant. Overall, which plant planted in this place has the best benefits?
